examples.gloss: I am tired, so I will sleep.
It is raining, so I will not go.
It was cheap, so I bought it.

usage: Because: gives the speaker's reason, usually subjective. 疲れたから寝る.
Before から the verb can be plain or polite: 食べますから.
Nouns and な-adjectives take だ: 雨だから.
It can end a sentence as a stand-alone answer: どうして? 疲れたから.

compare.difference: ので is more objective and softer, so it is better for polite explanations and requests: 遅れるので. から is more direct and can be followed by a command: 危ないから、やめて。
けど says 'but'. から says 'so'.
